manufacturer_or_packer.non_compliance_reason: Rule 6(1)(a) Explanation I requires a complete address at which the manufacturer can be identified and located. The pack names Hindustan Unilever Limited with a complete Mumbai address, but directs the reader to 'the first character(s) of the code' for the manufacturing unit, offering keys P) and Z). The only code printed on this face is Batch No. B240613A3, which begins with B and matches neither key, and the pack does not say which code is meant. The manufacturing unit address is therefore not resolvable from this image. Routed to human review, not FAIL: an unresolvable indirection is a gap in the evidence, not proof of an incomplete address. Source: rules-corpus/LMPC-2011__amended-to-2021-10-31__maharashtra-compilation.pdf, Rule 6(1)(a) Explanation I.

country_of_origin.non_compliance_reason: Rule 6(1)(aa) requires the name of the country of origin or manufacture or assembly 'in case of imported products'. Every address legible on this face is Indian and nothing on it indicates an imported product, so the obligation does not arise. Source: rules-corpus/LMPC-2011__amended-to-2021-10-31__maharashtra-compilation.pdf, Rule 6(1)(aa). The pack carries the statement even so; an obligation that does not arise is NOT_APPLICABLE, not PASS, even where the label happens to satisfy it.

notes: Back face of the carton. Two observations recorded verbatim and deliberately not characterised. First, the pack is Colgate-branded while naming Hindustan Unilever Limited as manufacturer, marketer and consumer-care contact; that is what the label says and this annotation transcribes it without inferring anything from it. Second, the manufacturing-unit indirection does not resolve: the keys printed are P) and Z), the batch code B240613A3 begins with B, and the pack says 'the code' without naming which code -- the incomplete_address case in this corpus, and the contrast to food_mdh_chicken_masala_100g_002 and food_aashirvaad_select_atta_1kg_002 where the same indirection does resolve. The unit sale price is on the correct statutory basis here: net quantity 100 g is less than one kilogram, so Rule 6(11) limb (i) requires a per-gram basis and the pack declares per g. No reference object of known size is in frame, so no millimetre letter or numeral height is measurable and no Rule 7 Table-I finding is supportable. pdp.is_measurable is false and every height field is null. The sample verdict is REVIEW for that reason alone, independently of what the declarations show.
